_comment: Curated alarm-name -> citation registry read by scripts/check_alarm_citations.py (#1959). Every CloudWatch alarm that has been in ALARM >72h must have an entry here (exact AlarmName key) naming the incident row or issue that explains it, or the /wrap gate flags it by name. Add an entry the same session a new long-red alarm is triaged; remove/replace one once the underlying issue closes AND the alarm has actually cleared live.

qa-smoke-warnings.note: #1958's chronic split deployed 2026-08-02 (ChronicWarnCount live) but the residual ALARMED set — 4 optional-metric nulls (sleep/hrv/glucose/hydration), the #1956 canary grant gap, the #1970 phase-stamp gap — still floored WarnCount at 5-8 nightly, so the alarm stayed structurally red. #2378 reclassifies those chronic; after its deploy WarnCount should drop to the genuine-signal set (character:receipt_replay + reader_truth verdicts). If still red a week after the #2378 deploy, the survivors are real findings — file them, don't re-cite.

life-platform-ingestion-dlq-messages.note: ALARM since 2026-08-03T12:04:26Z (verified via describe-alarm-history) — the whoop-data-ingestion EventBridge events that failed every hour from 12:00Z onward (first a 502 on the token endpoint, then repeated 'genuine auth failure' 400s the pre-fix breaker classifier never recognized) land here. The alarm + its urgent SNS route ('life-platform-alerts') worked correctly the whole time — remediation-dispatcher logged 'dispatched urgent_alarm' at 12:04:59Z — this was never a missing-machinery gap. Messages clear once #2069's classifier/rotation fix is deployed AND the credential is interactively re-authorized (owner action, concurrent with this filing) restores clean hourly runs; until then they are an accounted-for, expected byproduct of the known root cause, not a separate incident.

qa-smoke-failures.note: #2104's findings are fixed (closed 2026-08-05) but the alarm never got its 2 green nights — the 2026-08-05 scheduled run failed 2 content_truth with NEW causes: (1) whoop freshness (no DATE#2026-08-04 row) — the auth breaker re-latched 2026-08-04T00:00Z with 'refresh 400, unchanged refresh_token' (third credential loss; same owner re-auth path as #1934, carried on the owner list); (2) reader_truth high findings that are evidence, not new work: /api/sleep_detail claims total_sleep_hours with no night label while the whoop-based trend rows sit null during the outage (the #1968 class, evidence commented there), and Home's static 'sixteen prior climbs' lifetime count needs Matthew's factual call (owner list). Clears when whoop re-auths + the two reader_truth items are addressed + 2 green scheduled nights.

slo-source-freshness.citation: incident 2026-08-08 — measured, no code defect (see note)
slo-source-freshness.note: Red since 2026-08-05. MEASURED live 2026-08-08 against each source's own stale_hours in ingestion/source_registry.py, not inherited from a prior handover: food_delivery 133d (thr 14), measurements 132d (thr 60), macrofactor 45d (thr 4), strava 5d (thr 2), supplements 5d (thr 2), garmin 54d but PAUSED by ADR-074. Every one is a manual-drop or behavioural source with no writer running - i.e. the alarm is telling the truth and there is no code defect to fix. Kept RED on purpose: suppressing it would make the freshness SLO unable to report the condition it exists for. Re-measure before carrying this note forward; the set changes as Matthew drops files.

token-alarm-genesis-window-active.note: NOT A FAULT — by design. This is a boolean gauge sub-alarm carrying NO SNS action of its own (cdk/stacks/monitoring_stack.py, the TokenAlarmGenesisWindowActive block). ALARM means literally 'we are inside the genesis window', which the two composite alarms combine with the token-threshold breach so a genesis-week breach is digested rather than paged (#2116, after #1961's post-genesis rebuild pages). Cycle 13's genesis is 2026-08-10, so red since 2026-08-07 is the correct state. Expected to return to OK when the window closes; treat_missing_data=NOT_BREACHING so a stale gauge can never silently suppress a real page. If it is still ALARM well after the genesis window ends, THAT is the finding — file it, don't re-cite.
